hints: Focus on what redox really means here, a change in oxidation number due to gain or loss of electrons, not just any organic reaction.
Identify the reaction type for each pair first, addition to an alkene, dehydration, nucleophilic addition, and ester hydrolysis.
Check which pair has an element like bromine going from 0 to -1 while carbon is oxidised, that change in oxidation numbers signals redox.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as redox**

A redox reaction must show a change in oxidation number. One species is oxidised (loses electrons, oxidation number increases) and another is reduced (gains electrons, oxidation number decreases).

Rule to use:
$$\text{oxidation number change = redox}$$

**Name the organic reaction in each option**

Option A is electrophilic addition of $\text{Br}_2$ to the alkene $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$. Option B is acid-catalysed dehydration (elimination) of an alcohol to an alkene. Option C is nucleophilic addition of $\text{HCN}$ to the ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. Option D is acid hydrolysis of the ester $\text{HCO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$.

**Track oxidation numbers**

In A: $\text{Br}_2$ starts at 0 and becomes $\text{Br}^-$ in $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$, so bromine is reduced from 0 to -1 while the alkene carbons are oxidised. That is redox.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$$

**Confirm the others show no redox**

In B, C and D there is no oxidising or reducing agent and no change in oxidation number. Water is lost in dehydration, $\text{CN}^-$ just adds to $\text{C=O}$ in cyanohydrin formation, and water adds across the ester link in hydrolysis. So only the alkene plus bromine pair is redox.

options.A: Correct. This is electrophilic addition. $\text{Br}_2$ (oxidation number 0) is reduced to two $\text{C-Br}$ bonds where Br is -1, while the $\text{C=C}$ carbons are oxidised. Oxidation numbers change, so it is redox.
options.B: Not redox. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ undergoes dehydration to propene plus water. It is an acid-catalysed elimination, no electrons are gained or lost and oxidation numbers stay the same.
options.C: Not redox. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ with $\text{HCN}$ gives a cyanohydrin by nucleophilic addition. The $\text{CN}$ group simply adds to the carbonyl carbon, with no change in oxidation number for C, H, O or N.
options.D: Not redox. $\text{HCO}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ undergoes acid hydrolysis to methanoic acid and ethanol. It is a substitution (acyl) reaction with water adding across the ester bond, so no oxidation or reduction occurs.
